name: WideSearch

evaluation.harbor_aligned_metric: Mean Item F1 — Harbor parity uses the same Item F1 metric as the original WideSearch benchmark. Parity: claude-code@2.1.98+claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 achieves 0.539 ± 0.005 (original 0.538 ± 0.005) across 3 runs of 200 tasks. Delta 0.0009, well within agent non-determinism. Oracle Mean Item F1: 0.9996. Adapter PR: https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/pull/1232. Parity cost: ~$2000.

results_over_time.note: Full leaderboard from the WideSearch paper and official website, sorted by Mean Item F1 descending. 200 bilingual tasks, Avg@4 (average of 4 independent runs). Three agent paradigms: Single Agent, Multi-Agent (parallel sub-agents + aggregator), E2E System (end-to-end commercial search products). Item F1 is the most granular metric, evaluating individual cell accuracy against the ground-truth table.

notes:
WideSearch is a benchmark by ByteDance Seed for evaluating AI agents on broad information-seeking tasks. It contains 200 bilingual tasks (100 English, 100 Chinese) spanning 18 distinct industries, requiring agents to search, collect, and organize large-scale structured information into markdown tables.

Key characteristics:
- 200 tasks (100 EN + 100 ZH), 18 industries
- Evaluates operational scale and completeness, not cognitive difficulty ('I don't have time to do it' paradigm)
- Human annotators average 2.3 hours per task, consulting 44+ web pages
- Requires web search access (original benchmark uses ByteDance internal APIs; community must provide own search tools)
- Three key metrics: Success Rate (perfect match, extremely stringent), Row-level F1, Item-level F1
- Reporting: Avg@N (average of N trials) and Pass@N/Max@N (best of N trials)
- Three agent evaluation paradigms: Single Agent, Multi-Agent (parallel sub-agents + aggregator), E2E System

Harbor adapter details:
- Adapter builder: Yizhao Chen (yic138@ucsd.edu)
- Full 200 tasks adapted, 200 used for parity (100% sampling rate)
- Evaluation metrics ported from official WideSearch code (exact_match, number_near, url_match, date_near, llm_judge)
- LLM judge uses gpt-4.1 (configurable via WIDESEARCH_EVAL_MODEL)
- LLM-based primary key alignment for row matching
- Parity cost: ~$2000
- Oracle Mean Item F1: 0.9996 (not exactly 1.0 due to pipe characters in gold CSV causing lossy round-trip)
- Agent timeout: 1800 seconds (30 minutes)
- Temporal sensitivity: some tasks referencing 'latest' data may yield different correct answers over time
- Splits: full (200 tasks), prototype (5 tasks for development), parity (same as full)
